paragraphs: On Thursday after lunch, the Explorers met in the school library. Teacher Kim put a big poster on the wall. "The school has a poster competition," she said. "All the pupils can enter, and the subject is Animals in Our Park." "Please give me your posters on Monday." Leo and May sat at a table with a pencil and a big sheet of paper. They wanted to make a poster for the competition. The other children were busy with their own ideas.

"Let's draw a leopard," said Leo. "A spotted leopard looks great on a poster." "I don't agree," said May. "There are no leopards in our park." "That is true," said Leo, "but a leopard is more exciting." "Maybe," said May, "but the poster is about our park." "Let's draw an animal from the park."

May went to the shelf and took a guidebook about the nature park. "Look at this page," she said. "There is a green frog, a red squirrel, and a spotted deer." "A spotted deer?" asked Leo. "I like it, because it has spots like a leopard!" "Now I agree with you," said May. "The deer is real, and it is beautiful."

"What is a good title?" asked May. "I think 'Spots in Our Park' is good," said Leo. "I prefer 'Our Spotted Deer'," said May. "It is clear, and it tells people about the animal." "I see your point," said Leo. "But my title is funny, and funny posters are good." May smiled. "Then let's use both," she said. "The big title is 'Spots in Our Park', and the small title is 'Our Spotted Deer'."

Teacher Kim came to the table and looked at the paper. "You need a short letter with your poster," she said. May wrote at the top of a page, "Dear Teacher Kim," "I can't draw a deer," said Leo. "I will worry all week." "Don't worry," said May. "I will draw the deer, and you will draw the trees and the letters." "Great idea!" said Leo. They worked together until the end of the club hour. The poster was not finished, but they were happy with the plan. They wanted to work on it again on Friday, because the posters were due on Monday.
text.summary: Leo and May make a poster for a school competition. They disagree about the animal and the title, and then they agree on a spotted deer.
